_comment: Generated by scripts/generate-town-plans.py --write; edit the blueprints
there, not the steps here. See docs/AI_ARCHITECTURE.md, town plans.
Authored settlement blueprints, in the spirit of a castle plan rather than
an optimiser. Steps are built in order, each one skipped when that building
already stands in its slot or cannot be afforded yet, so a plan degrades
into a partial town instead of stalling.
Offsets are metres in the settlement's own frame, relative to its base
anchor: negative z faces the enemy, positive z is the rear. Nothing may sit
within 9m of the anchor, which the base itself occupies.
A step's optional 'rotation' is degrees in that same frame: 0 runs a wall
along x (parallel to the front), 90 runs it along z. Wall links stand 2m
apart along their line; a wall_gate spans 9m of a run and is the only way
through a closed ring. A circuit is listed as one growing run: the front
gate, then links outward along both arms, round the corners, down the
flanks, closing at the rear, so any prefix of it is a wall with two ends.
Caps: 128 wall links, 12 towers, 12 homes, 4 gates per plan.
An unknown building name is skipped with a warning; an unknown plan name
falls back to the built-in layout table.
